decisions.reason: The breakpoint changes responsive placement to prevent overlap but does not change the hero text-emphasis requirement; the responsive behavior is already owned by the source Requirement.
A landing-page-specific breakpoint does not necessarily revise the reusable general breakpoint guidance or its stated basis.
The breakpoint does not change the selected visual concepts, theme, colors, font, or other visual-direction attributes.
The responsive breakpoint does not alter the shared dark-theme decision or its non-switchable behavior.
Preventing hero text and image overlap does not change the landing-page sections, copy plan, sequence, or section order.
The breakpoint does not change whether the landing page requires a sign-up button.
Adding a breakpoint in styles.css is compatible with the existing build stack and does not change the selected HTML and Tailwind implementation approach.
The hero-specific responsive breakpoint does not necessarily change the Cognito sign-in branding, required elements, or use of the landing-page background.
The breakpoint does not affect the decision to omit navigation from the landing-page header.
A breakpoint introduced for the landing-page hero does not change the separate admin workspace shell styling requirement.
The landing-page hero breakpoint does not change the provisioning wizard's independent responsive variables, styling values, or unresolved accent choice.
The breakpoint specifically addresses overlap between the hero text and image and does not change the footer's content, navigation, placement, or shared-component semantics.
